transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yeah. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just can't keep my mind on one single thing anymore. Like, I work at this freight warehouse, and I'll be right in the middle of a count, but if a beeper goes off, or a forklift alarm sounds, or somebody is just moving a pallet nearby, I get totally pulled off my count. 

Actually, speaking of the pallets, they just started using these new heavy-duty plastic ones instead of the wooden ones, and my coworker Dave was saying they're supposed to be better for the environment or something? I don't know, I took a couple of environmental science classes back when I was doing some college courses in my thirties, and I remember learning that half that stuff is just corporate greenwashing anyway. But Dave just will not stop talking about it, he thinks he's an expert now. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right... the warehouse. So yeah, I get pulled away by every little noise or distraction, and then by the time I look back down, I realize I've gone and put the completely wrong numbers into the inventory system.
Do you find yourself getting distracted easily in other parts of your life, like at home or while driving, or is it mostly just at work?

At home or driving? Um... well, with driving, I have this older Honda, and honestly, the radio in that thing has a mind of its own lately. I'll be on the highway and suddenly it just switches from the classic rock station to pure static. It's so annoying. 

My brother-in-law said he could look at the wiring for me, but he’s always saying he’ll fix things and then never actually gets around to it. Like last Thanksgiving, he promised to fix my sister's garbage disposal and ended up flooding the entire cabinet under the sink. Ruined a whole box of her good holiday napkins. They had those little embroidered turkeys on them, too, she was so mad. So I definitely don't let him touch my car. 

But... wait, I'm sorry, what were you asking about my driving? I don't really know if I get distracted doing that, I haven't really noticed.
Do you have trouble staying focused on tasks or activities at home or in other situations, like following through with chores, reading, or listening to someone speak?

Chores at home? Um, I guess I haven't really noticed if I have trouble focusing on them. I mean, I live alone, so it's just me making the mess and me cleaning it up. I did try to read this book the other day, though. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she's always trying to get me to join her book club. She gave me this mystery novel, said it was a real page-turner. 

But honestly, I couldn't get past the first chapter because the main character was a baker, and it made me crave blueberry muffins so bad. I actually ended up going to the grocery store right then to get muffin mix. The store was packed, though, because they were having a sale on those big packs of paper towels. You know, the ones that take up half your cart? I always wonder where people even store those in their houses. I barely have room under my sink because of all the cleaning supplies I bought last year and never used. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, reading and chores. Yeah, I don't really know if I have trouble focusing on that stuff. I just sort of do things when I feel like it.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or avoiding tasks that require you to keep your mind focused for a long time, like paying bills or planning your day?

Organizing tasks? Well, like paying bills, I mean... I still get paper bills for some things, like the electric company. They keep sending those little inserts with the bill, you know, telling you how to save energy by switching to LED bulbs. I actually bought a whole pack of those LED bulbs at the hardware store a few months ago because the guy there said they last for like ten years. He was this young kid, probably still in high school, wearing this bright orange apron that was way too big for him. It reminded me of when my nephew started working at a home improvement store, he used to complain about the uniform all the time. He ended up quitting and getting a job at a doggy daycare, which is funny because he used to be terrified of dogs when he was little. 

Anyway... wait, what did you ask me? Something about avoiding tasks? I don't know, I guess I just haven't really thought about if I avoid things like that.
Do you often find yourself making mistakes or overlooking small details when doing tasks, even if you're trying to pay attention?

Mistakes? Overlooking things? Well, actually, yeah, that's kind of what brings me in here. I just can't seem to keep my mind on one thing anymore, especially at work. I work at this big warehouse, and there's always something going on. Like, I'll be trying to count the stock, and then a forklift alarm will go off, or someone's moving a pallet, or a beeper sounds, and my attention just snaps right to it. 

The other day, this guy Jimmy—he drives the forklift on the morning shift—he dropped a whole pallet of those giant cans of baked beans. You wouldn't believe the mess. It smelled like barbecue sauce in that aisle for three days straight. Jimmy's a nice guy, though, he always brings in donuts on Fridays. He gets them from this little bakery downtown that makes these amazing maple bacon bars. I don't even usually like bacon on sweet things, but they do it just right, you know? It's like the perfect mix of salty and sweet. 

But anyway, what happens is, I get pulled off the count by all that noise, and then I realize I've put the completely wrong numbers into the inventory system. It's really starting to become a problem.
Do you find that these issues with distraction and losing track of tasks happen in places other than work, like when you're at home or spending time with friends or family?

Well, yeah, it's definitely not just at work. I mean, at the warehouse, I've had to go back and double-check things with my supervisor because of those inventory errors. He's been pretty patient about it, honestly. His name is Greg, and he's been working there for like twenty years. He's got this huge collection of vintage lunchboxes in his office—like, real metal ones from the seventies. He's got a Star Wars one that he said is worth a couple hundred bucks now. I remember having a Peanuts lunchbox when I was a kid, the one with Snoopy on the red doghouse. I used to carry a thermos of tomato soup in it, but the lid always leaked, so everything smelled like tomatoes. 

But anyway, yeah, at home it's happening too. My husband just retired, which you'd think would be great, right? More time together, relaxing. But we've just been arguing so much lately. It feels like we're just walking around each other, trying to avoid setting each other off, instead of actually settling into this retirement thing. He bought this massive RV right after he retired—one of those ones that looks like a tour bus. He wants to drive to all the national parks, but I don't know, those things get terrible gas mileage, and I get motion sickness if I read in the car. 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, distraction at home. Yeah, it's definitely causing some friction with him, too.
Looking back, would you say these kinds of attention problems and difficulty staying focused have been with you for most of your life, even going back to when you were a child or in school?

Most of my life? No, I don't think so. I mean, I was pretty good in school, at least until I got to college. I only went for a few semesters anyway before I started working. I took this one psychology class where the professor made us keep a dream journal. He had this wild curly hair, kind of looked like Albert Einstein if he wore Hawaiian shirts. I remember writing down this recurring dream I had about being chased by a giant rolling doughnut. It was always jelly-filled, which is weird because I prefer glazed. Actually, the bakery near my house makes the best glazed doughnuts, they're so light they just melt in your mouth. The owner, Maria, she's been running the place for thirty years. Her daughter just had twins, a boy and a girl. 

Anyway... no, I don't remember having these kinds of focus problems back then. It really just feels like it's been lately that I can't keep my thoughts straight.
Do you often feel restless or find yourself needing to be constantly moving, like you can't sit still for very long?

Restless? Yeah, actually, that's been happening a lot. Usually, after a long shift at the warehouse, I'm just completely worn out, you know? Moving freight all day really takes it out of you. But lately, I come home and I'm just buzzing. Sitting on the couch to watch TV or relax just feels completely impossible right now. 

So instead of resting, I've been tearing through the house. Like the other night, I started completely reorganizing the kitchen cabinets. And I found so many plastic containers that don't even have matching lids anymore. I swear the dishwasher just eats them. Or my husband puts them on the bottom rack and melts them. He actually did that to my favorite Pyrex mixing bowl once—it was this vintage green one, the Spring Blossom pattern, that my grandmother gave me when I got my first apartment. She had the whole matching set, even those little rectangular glass refrigerator dishes. She used to make this incredible three-bean salad and keep it in those dishes. God, I miss her cooking. She put celery seed in it, which sounds weird, but it gave it this perfect little crunch. 

But anyway, yeah, I just couldn't sit down. So after I finished the kitchen cabinets, I went straight out to the garage and started sorting all the plastic storage bins out there. I just had to keep moving, I couldn't stop.
